bluf: Assembly is Stagwell's global omnichannel media network, 3,000+ people, that calls itself a tech company and leads with STAGE, a data and experience operating system it says lifts brand performance by more than 30%. The record shows it winning and keeping enterprise media accounts (Hyatt in April 2025, SXSW London kept in May 2026) and folding in ADK Global in July 2025. Its own house is quiet: no Google or LinkedIn ads, nothing published in 12 months. A rival should know the Horus read puts it at Neutral 0.1, most exposed to the hollowing of the agency middle, with 11 of 13 clients names only.
doing:
The positioning line reads: global omnichannel media agency that calls itself a tech company, using its STAGE data engine to turn brand experience into brand performance. In plain words: a holdco media buyer selling itself as a data platform. The headline claim is that STAGE lifts brand performance by more than 30%.

The services list pairs platform lines (STAGE Experience Engine, Brand Performance Planning) with delivery lines (Digital Commerce, Global Delivery, Search, Social) and a Political Practice the About page calls the first and only fully operational political practice at a media agency. Data & Measurement is the sole lead line at 3: STAGE leads the homepage, and Royal Canin and Mars are analytics cases. Core lines at 2 are Paid Search (Ralph Lauren PMax and Simon search cases), Paid Social (Mandarin Oriental, Mastercard and Simon on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube), Programmatic & CTV (Hyatt global paid media AOR; CTV in the Simon campaign) and Retail Media (a Digital Commerce practice; Mars and Royal Canin commerce cases). Proprietary names: STAGE, Brand Performance Planning, Advocacy Consulting Technology (ACT) and Clean Media Lab. The only partner listed is Google Marketing Platform.

The AI posture is platform talk plus playbooks: STAGE is pitched as an AI enabled operating system and it publishes agentic commerce and AI search playbooks on feeds, schema and AI native ad formats, yet AI Search / GEO and AI Automation each score 1.

Moves in date order: April 2025, Hyatt picked it as global paid media agency of record; May 2025, Jason Lim named first Chief Media Officer for North America; July 2025, combined with ADK Global to form an Asia Pacific challenger agency; May 2026, kept SXSW London as agency of record after a competitive review. The record lists no pricing model. Conspicuously absent for a network of this size: SEO at 1, content and PR, email and CRM and B2B at 0, and no jobs.
clients:
The Radar files Assembly's clients as enterprise, its home region as the US, its verticals as Luxury retail, Fashion & apparel, Beauty & skincare, Retail & real estate, Luxury hospitality, Pet care, Financial services, CPG and Political & advocacy.

The needs read counts 13 clients: 2 observed and 11 names only, and both observed codes are thin. SXSW London is coded PR, reputation and content from the release retaining it as agency of record after a competitive review; the code appears to key on 'review'. amika is coded local and lead generation from its news slug 'amika taps assembly to lead integrated media program', apparently keyed on 'lead'. Both are likely media mandates (inferred, moderate confidence). Each mix share, 0.562 PR and 0.437 leads, rests on one client.

Two of the 11 say more than a name: the Hyatt slug reads 'paid global media agency of record' and the Pipedrive slug 'global media partner', mandates the read leaves uncoded. Capability notes credit Ralph Lauren PMax, Simon search and CTV, Mandarin Oriental and Mastercard paid social, and Mars and Royal Canin analytics and commerce: paid and data work, inferred. American Eagle, La Mer and Brooks Running are bare names, need inferred from the sold mix.

Four clients sit on other tracked books: Mars with bounteous and valtech, Mandarin Oriental with valtech, Mastercard with transmission, Brooks Running with tinuiti. All four are names only.

Horus has Assembly best placed for KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better): the luxury, beauty and CPG accounts are likely, moderate confidence, to buy defensible measurement from whoever holds their media, the STAGE pitch. Under KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out), its main exposure, the paid hours in the Hyatt and Pipedrive mandates have a roughly even chance of repricing within the edition.
house: Say and do: 1 of 4 tested lines is practised on its own house. Paid social is corroborated by a LinkedIn Insight pixel on its site. Paid search is contradicted: it sells paid search and runs no Google ads of its own (Transparency Center status none, 0 ads). LinkedIn advertising is contradicted: 1,700 ads match the name query across all advertisers and the first page shows 24 cards, but none are its own; Assembly Culture (1) is excluded as a near name advertiser. Publishing cadence is contradicted: a blog exists but nothing in its sitemap of 181 URLs was updated in 90 or 365 days; 5 of those URLs are AI topics. There is no llms.txt and no AI crawler is blocked, so its AI search playbooks sit on a site that gives answer engines no map. The tag stack is GTM, GA4 and LinkedIn Insight on Webflow; no test tools or ABM stack are listed.
market:
The Horus read scores a tailwind index of 0.1, Neutral band. It is best placed for KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better, net 0.257), driven by Data & Measurement, and for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), driven by AI Search / GEO. It is most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out, net -0.675) through Paid Search and Paid Social. Best fit is The Walled Oasis at 47/100. The read has it making P2 and P4, partial on P1, unknown on P5, absent on P6, P7 and P8.

The Monsoon read scores 60.1, Onshore wind band: migration 80.1 against displacement 40.1, so the hours move but the book does not buy on price. Data & Measurement (8) and Paid Search (7) carry the most movable hours. The work would go 59% to South and Southeast Asia, 16% to Eastern Europe and 16% to Latin America. The footprint is observed: hub offices in Warsaw, Cairo, Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai, Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok and Ho Chi Minh City, and no onshore claim.
openings:
Lead with the quiet house. It sells paid search and runs no Google ads; it sells paid social and runs no LinkedIn ads; its blog is idle for 12 months. A rival showing its own live campaigns and a working publishing machine makes the contrast; very likely, high confidence. The falsifier: a live Assembly Google or LinkedIn campaign and fresh sitemap dates at the next compile.

The shared clients are contestable: Mars sits on bounteous and valtech books, Mandarin Oriental on valtech, Mastercard on transmission, Brooks Running on tinuiti, and all four are names only; likely, moderate confidence, these accounts are already multi agency and open to a measurement or commerce pitch.

The delivery footprint is listed (Warsaw, Cairo, Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai, Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok, Ho Chi Minh City), so an onshore pitch has something concrete to point at, though with displacement at 40.1 the book is unlikely to switch on price alone. No public pricing (P5 unknown) means an outcome priced offer forces a conversation it cannot have in public; no ads tested inside AI assistants (P8 absent) despite its AI search playbooks means the first rival to show assistant ad results likely sets the price.
watch: I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: output or outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco would deepen its KJ6 exposure, and Stagwell's own disclosures are the ones to read.
I4, Meta Q3 2026 average price per ad, next reading late October 2026: a print at or above +5% continues walled garden inflation and adds to its KJ5 exposure through paid social and programmatic.
The July 2025 combination with ADK Global: any named Asia Pacific client win or office change would show whether the challenger agency is landing accounts.

The May 2026 retention of SXSW London after a competitive review: a further retention or loss among the shared clients (Mars, Mandarin Oriental, Mastercard, Brooks Running) would show which way the book is moving.
The next Radar compile: the dossier is only as fresh as 28 September 2026, and a new compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients.
